findings.highlight: I can only sigh in admiration.
findings.evidenceJa: へえ、と感心するしかない
findings.governingReading: Shirou can only respond with an impressed “huh.”
findings.explanation: The English invents a sigh, changing a small reaction of wonder into an exhalation often associated with weariness.

findings.highlight: I should be able to persuade people in the neighborhood that she is a relative of Kiritsugu. …Well, I would have to do so anyway.
findings.evidenceJa: ご近所の目を誤魔化せるだろう。……って、誤魔化し通すしかないんだけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou plans to pass Saber off as Kiritsugu’s relative to fool the neighbors, then corrects himself: he has no choice but to keep the deception going.
findings.explanation: Persuade removes the false-cover element, and the closing paraphrase loses his self-correction about sustaining the deception.
